summary: Michael Carrithers works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Wesleyan University and earned his doctorate at Oxford. He held lecturing posts at Oxford and LSE before becoming Lecturer, Reader, and Professor of Anthropology at Durham University.

Michael Comans specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and completed his doctorate under Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University. He held positions at the University of Sydney and Sri Venkateswara Temple.
Michael J. Conway is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He serves as Lecturer of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and is affiliated with the Otani Academic Society.

Michael Coulson specialized in Indology and linguistics. He completed his B.A. at Trinity College, Oxford, and his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford. From around 1965 to 1975, he served as Lecturer and Head of the Sanskrit Department at Edinburgh.

Michael Eido Luetchford works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied electronic engineering at the University of Bradford, studied under traditional teacher Gudo Wafu Nishijima from 1977 to 2007, and founded Windbell Publications.

Michael Fertig was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Würzburg under Othmar Frank. He later taught Latin at the University of Passau in 1846 and served as Rector of Hans-Carossa-Gymnasium Landshut from 1855 to 1869.

Michael Friedrich is a sinologist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich, where he served as Wissenschaftlicher Assistent. From 1994 to 2021, he held a professorship at the University of Hamburg.
Michael G. Morony works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley and UCLA, where he became a professor in 1974.

Michael Haberlandt worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna under Friedrich Müller and Georg Bühler, later becoming an ao. Professor there and Director of the Natural History Museum, Vienna in 1911.

Michael Hahn was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. He held posts at the University of Bonn and was Professor of Indology and Tibetology at Marburg from 1988 to 2007.
Michael Harack is a scholar in religious studies and sinology. He earned his Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn.
Michael Hookham is active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa in 1965 and founded the Longchen Foundation.

Michael Hutt works in Indology and linguistics. He completed his BA and doctorate at the University of London. At SOAS, he served as a postdoctoral fellow, Head of the South Asia Department, and Associate Dean.

Michael I. Como works in religious studies, Japanology, and sinology. Advised by Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt, he joined Columbia University, where he is attested as Tōshū Fukami Associate Professor of Shinto Studies.

Michael J. Sweet specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, studying under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Geshe Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Legden, and others, later serving as clinical assistant professor in psychiatry there.
Michael J. Tetreault works in religious studies and philosophy. He earned a Master of Arts degree at San Diego State University under the supervision of Sandra A. Wawrytko.

Michael J. Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a B.Soc.Sc. from the University of Cape Town, an M.A. from UC Santa Barbara, and completed his doctoral studies under William F. Powell.

Michael Janda works in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Jochem Schindler and completed his PhD under Heiner Eichner at the University of Vienna, followed by a Habilitation at Zurich. In 2002, he took a professorship at Münster.

Michael Jansen was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Bonn, RWTH Aachen, Rome, and Delhi, he was Dean of Architecture at RWTH Aachen, founding rector of GUtech in Oman, and President of Research Centre Indian Ocean.

Michael Jerryson specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and earned his PhD at UC Santa Barbara under Mark Juergensmeyer. He taught at Eckerd College and Youngstown State University.
